title: The writer's purpose and audience
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Every text is written for a reason and for someone. Knowing the writer's purpose and audience helps you understand why it is written the way it is.
A writer's purpose is usually to INFORM (give facts), to PERSUADE (change your mind), or to ENTERTAIN (enjoy).

steps: A news report giving facts → to inform.
A poster saying 'Save water!' → to persuade.

blocks.question: A poster that says 'Vote for cleaner beaches!' has what main purpose?
blocks.explain: It is trying to change your mind and get you to act, so its purpose is to persuade.
blocks.rule: A writer's purpose is to inform, to persuade, or to entertain.

practiceItems.prompt: purpose of a text that gives facts
purpose of a text that tries to convince you
purpose of a recipe that tells you the steps

blocks.content: The audience is WHO the text is written for — for example, young children, parents, or shoppers.

blocks.question: A book with big pictures and very simple words is written for which audience?
blocks.explain: Big pictures and simple words suit young children, so they are the audience.
blocks.rule: The audience is the group of readers a text is written for.

practiceItems.prompt: who a text is written for is its ___
a text with simple words and pictures is for young ___
the reason a text is written is its ___
an advertisement's purpose is usually to ___

blocks.question: A text is full of lines like 'Buy now! Best price! Don't miss out!' What is the writer's purpose?
options: To persuade you to buy — it uses selling words
blocks.explain: A writer writes to inform, to persuade, or to entertain. All these urgent selling phrases are meant to make you buy, so the purpose is to persuade. The audience is a possible customer.
blocks.rule: Writing aims to inform, persuade, or entertain.
blocks.principle: The writer's word choices reveal their purpose.
canonical_solution: The text uses urgent selling words
Selling words push you to act
So the purpose is to persuade you to buy

rubric.look_for: reads the selling language as a clue

misconceptions.coach: It is not just giving facts — it pushes you to buy.
The selling words aim to persuade, not amuse.

practiceItems.prompt: writing that makes you buy has the purpose to
writing that gives facts aims to
writing that makes you laugh aims to

blocks.content: Ask 'why was this written?' for the purpose, and 'who is it for?' for the audience. Let's practise!
